label: Set Theory
shortDescription: The foundation of modern mathematics: sets, ordinals, cardinals, and independence.
modulesDescription: Read the set-theory chapters in order, or jump directly to the topic you need.
ogTitle: Learn Set Theory for Free | CalcPath
ogDescription: Master naive and axiomatic set theory, Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms, ordinals, cardinals, the axiom of choice and its equivalents, forcing, independence results, and advanced topics like large cardinals and Martin's axiom — with ELI5 explanations, worked examples, and practice questions.
courseDescription: A complete set theory course covering foundations (sets, elements, subsets, unions), the ZFC axioms, ordinals and cardinals, transfinite methods, the axiom of choice and equivalents (Zorn, well-ordering, Tychonoff), independence and forcing, and advanced topics in descriptive set theory and forcing axioms. Features ELI5 intuition, step-by-step worked examples, common mistakes, and practice problems for each lesson.

topics.title: Naive Set Theory
topics.description: Sets, membership and the double-inclusion method that follows from extensionality; why membership and inclusion are genuinely different relations; Russell's paradox derived in full, with the failing assumption located and separation shown to repair it; power sets with the count 2 to the n; Cantor's theorem by the diagonal set; and the union, intersection, distributive and De Morgan laws proved by element chasing, including arbitrary indexed families.

topics.title: ZFC Axioms
topics.description: The nine axioms and what each one buys: extensionality and the uniqueness of the empty set; separation blocking Russell and proving there is no universal set; intersection and difference needing no axioms of their own; the Kuratowski ordered pair with its degenerate case; Cartesian products from power set and separation; foundation forbidding membership cycles; the von Neumann naturals satisfying the Peano axioms; the cumulative hierarchy with the sizes of its finite stages; and replacement as a schema reaching sets separation cannot.

topics.title: Ordinals & Cardinals
topics.description: Von Neumann ordinals, transitive and well-ordered by membership; the Burali-Forti paradox proved in full; every well-order isomorphic to a unique ordinal; ordinal arithmetic shown non-commutative by 1 plus omega against omega plus 1; countability of the integers and rationals by explicit bijections; Cantor's theorem; Cantor-Schroder-Bernstein by the chain partition, with its freedom from choice explained; cardinal arithmetic and the one hard operation; transfinite induction and recursion with the limit step treated separately; and the continuum hypothesis as independent rather than unknown.

topics.title: Axiom of Choice & Equivalents
topics.description: Finite choice proved in ZF, so that what the axiom actually adds is clear; choice equivalent to every surjection splitting; Zorn's lemma applied to bases and maximal ideals; Zorn implies well-ordering implies choice, both proved; Vitali's non-measurable set constructed in full with the countable-additivity contradiction spelled out; Banach-Tarski stated precisely and outlined honestly; the countable and dependent choice hierarchy; and why the independence of the axiom does not license using it and denying it in the same argument.

topics.title: Independence & Forcing
topics.description: Why every independence result is conditional on the consistency of ZFC, via Godel's second theorem; the constructible universe, its definable well-ordering and its absoluteness; forcing posets, dense sets and generic filters, with the Cohen conditions proved dense and the generic real proved different from every ground-model real; the continuum hypothesis settled by Godel and Cohen; inaccessible cardinals giving models of ZFC and so unprovable in it; measurable implies inaccessible; and the consistency-strength ladder.

topics.title: Advanced Set Theory
topics.description: The Borel hierarchy as the smallest sigma-algebra on the opens, closing at exactly omega-one; analytic sets as continuous images of Baire space, and where the projective hierarchy escapes ZFC; determinacy, with the axiom of determinacy proved to contradict choice and the Banach-Mazur game characterising meagreness; Martin's axiom, what it decides about the continuum, and the proper forcing axiom; Ramsey's theorem in both versions with Sierpinski's colouring showing the continuum fails; the sunflower lemma; and clubs, stationary sets and Fodor's lemma.
